shared_elements: upright stone slab as carved surface
shallow low-relief / incised carving in pale tan stone
horizontal lines dividing the surface into registers
a band of repeated small motifs running horizontally near the top
justification: Both are upright pale stone slabs organised into stacked horizontal registers, each with a row of repeated near-identical creatures across the top and profile birds and animals below, which is a genuine compositional echo. The difference is decisive in execution and density: A is finely incised, crowded with hundreds of small standardised sign-like marks and seated human figures, while B carries only a handful of large, boldly modelled relief animals on a plain ground with no script-like matrix.
